America's New Airfields and Helipads, 1981–2026

Every airport, heliport and seaplane base in the FAA's register, lit up in the month it was added. The 6,775 sites already listed by 1981 glow faintly from the start; the 11,306 added since then appear one by one, and more than four in ten of them are heliports.

Data: FAA National Airspace System Resources (NASR) 28-day subscription, airport base file (APT_BASE), effective 29 October 2026; US government data, public domain. The date shown is the FAA's activation date: in the FAA's words, "the month and year that the facility was added to the NFDC airport database. Note: this information is only available for those facilities opened since 1981." So this is when a site entered the register, which can differ from when it first opened; sites dated before 1981 are shown as already listed in 1981. Only facilities operating today are included: airfields that closed are no longer in the file, so the map shows today's sites by the date they were added, not every site that ever existed. Left out: 288 sites marked closed; 852 with no activation date; 210 in US territories or with no state; 2 in the far-western Aleutians and 1 in the far-northwest Hawaiian Islands, outside the map insets. Map: Highcharts map collection (US states, with Alaska and Hawaii as insets). · Highcharts.com
